classification.difficultyReason: Introduce an unsupplied altitude and use isosceles symmetry to halve the base, then apply inverse cosine and the angle sum to recover all three angles.

content.prompt: An isosceles triangle has base length 10 cm and the other two sides are each of length 6 cm. Find the angles in the triangle, giving your answers correct to the nearest degree.

answer.short:
$34^\circ$, $113^\circ$, $34^\circ$.

Bisect the base with a perpendicular from the apex and use cosine to find a base angle.
answer.worked:
Draw the perpendicular from the apex to the base. In an isosceles triangle this bisects the base, giving two right-angled triangles with base 5 cm and hypotenuse 6 cm. Let each base angle be $\alpha$ and the apex angle be $\beta$.

$$\begin{align*}\cos\alpha&=\frac{5}{6}\\\alpha&=\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)\\\alpha&\approx34^\circ\\\beta&=180^\circ-2\cos^{-1}\left(\frac{5}{6}\right)\\\beta&\approx113^\circ\end{align*}$$

The angles are $34^\circ$, $113^\circ$ and $34^\circ$, rounded independently to the nearest degree.
